newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - September 25.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Wednesday.
- A man being held in custody in London after this week's police raids is believed to be a close associate of the County Monaghan man reputed to be the IRA chief-of-staff.
- Security arrangements for EU meetings during Ireland's presidency are to be reviewed after farmers broke through police barriers to a hotel where farm ministers were staying on Tuesday.
- The U.S. Federal Reserve Board surprised Irish financial markets by leaving U.S. interest rates unchanged.
- Irish market research firm MRBI allowed British market information company Taylor Nelson AGB to take a 72 percent controlling stake on Tuesday.
- Four objections have been made to Irish planning body An Bord Pleanala on the Lisheen mining project in Tipperary.
- The 27-year-old Irishman shot dead by police in London last Monday was convicted of defrauding Bank of Ireland of almost 75,000 punts in 1987.

- Trade unions representing staff at Irish telecommunications firm Telecom Eireann have expressed their "extreme concern" at the provisions in the new Telecommunications Bill which plans to halve the number of worker directors on the Board.
- A trade pact was signed in Dublin on Tuesday between Ireland and the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), the largest republic in the Russian Federation after Russia itself.
- Airport charges and ferry tickets in County Cork could rise in cost if the EU goes ahead with its plans to abolish duty free shops in 1999, a meeting was told on Tuesday.
